northstar-atlas-release.title: Northstar ships Atlas 1.0 with a promise of byte-for-byte replay
northstar-atlas-release.dek: Full coverage: the Seattle developer-tools firm says any recorded run of its simulator can be reproduced exactly from its seed.
body: Northstar released version 1.0 of Atlas on Wednesday, a simulation runtime that removes the wall clock, host randomness and unordered iteration from the code it runs so that a failure can be replayed rather than reproduced by repetition. The company published the source alongside the release and has not disclosed revenue or headcount. Reuters filed the release as a two-minute wire story, while The Verge ran a longer feature built around an interview with engineering manager Carol Nakamura.
Source: Reuters, The Verge. Read the wire story at http://reuters.com/2026/northstar-atlas-determinism and the feature at http://theverge.com/2026/atlas-determinism

northstar-latency-outage.title: Northstar restores service after a four-hour latency incident
northstar-latency-outage.dek: The company blamed a scheduler regression and published a postmortem the same week.
body: Northstar's hosted service returned to normal latency on Thursday after roughly four hours of degraded response times that the company traced to a scheduler regression. Reuters carried the confirmation from the company; the status page and the engineering blog both published timelines within the week.
Source: Reuters. Read the confirmation at http://reuters.com/2026/northstar-latency-incident
